title: WooCommerce backorders for B2B: how to set lead times, cap orders and avoid overselling

linkedin.post:
A buyer orders a pallet of one part.
You have a handful on the shelf.

Your store says yes anyway.

No warning to the buyer. No limit. Nothing stops it.

Three things most owners miss:

1️⃣ There is no backorder status on the order.
Your team can't filter for the risky ones.

2️⃣ The one alert goes to your staff, not the buyer.
If nobody reads that mailbox, nobody knows.

3️⃣ The link to your stock system can switch itself off.
It happens after more than five failed deliveries in a row. Then it stops sending.

Try this today.

Place one test order past zero on a product you stock.

Then read what your team receives. And what the buyer sees.

A backorder is a promise.

Does your store keep it?

instagram.caption:
🚨 Your buyer ordered a pallet. You had a handful of units.

Your store accepted the order anyway. Now someone has to explain the delay.

Here are 4 stages of a backorder, seen from your buyer's side:

1️⃣ The promise
The order goes through, and the buyer may see no delay at all.

2️⃣ The wait
Without a date, the buyer has nothing to plan around.

3️⃣ The surprise
Stock drops below zero, and your team gets one quiet email.

4️⃣ The fix
A date you can keep, a limit you set and a mailbox someone reads.

💡 A backorder is a promise. One test order shows you what your buyer and your team really see.

cards.label: The fix
cards.detail: A date, a limit, a mailbox

slides.alt: B2B buyer at a desk checking a confirmed order on screen while a warehouse shelf behind shows only a few boxes left.

slides.headline: The Cart Says Yes
slides.body: A buyer adds a large quantity of one part. Only a few units sit on your shelf, yet the order goes through with no warning.
slides.alt: Buyer confirming a large parts order on a laptop while a warehouse shelf nearby holds only a few units.

slides.headline: Then The Buyer Waits
slides.body: A notice that only says backordered gives no date to plan around. The buyer expects every unit this week and calls sales.
slides.alt: Frustrated buyer on the phone at a desk, checking a calendar with no delivery date marked for the order.

slides.headline: Your Team Hears Late
slides.body: Stock drops below zero. The only signal is one email to your staff, and it goes to a mailbox that may not be read.
slides.alt: Warehouse manager looking at an empty shelf while an unread staff inbox sits open on a nearby computer.

slides.headline: Fix It Around The Promise
slides.body: Give a ship-by date from a confirmed supplier order. Set your own limit, and make sure someone reads the mailbox.
slides.alt: Operations manager and warehouse lead reviewing a supplier delivery date on a printed order beside shelves.
